title: Etaleness descends to a stage over an affine limit of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A space is quasi-compact if every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback to every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. An affine morphism is representable by schemes and has affine source after every affine scheme test. Local finite presentation and local finite type are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]; finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness.  An open subspace is represented on each scheme test by an open subscheme [def-a1-space-open-subspace]; a closed immersion is represented on each scheme test by a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Etale morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(B_i)$ an inverse system with affine transitions and limit $B$, and fix $i_0\in I$. Assume $B_{i_0}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $f_{i_0}:X_{i_0}\to Y_{i_0}$ be a locally finitely presented morphism over $B_{i_0}$, with $X_{i_0}$ and $Y_{i_0}$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For $i\geq i_0$, write $f_i:X_{i_0}\times_{B_{i_0}}B_i\to Y_{i_0}\times_{B_{i_0}}B_i$ for its base change, and let $f$ be its base change to $B$. If $f$ is etale, there is $i\geq i_0$ such that $f_i$ is etale. No scheme hypothesis is imposed on the bases or the spaces.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence], the map $f_{i_0}$ is quasi-compact: its source is quasi-compact and its target is quasi-separated. Choose an affine scheme $V_0$ and a representable surjective etale map $b_0:V_0\to Y_{i_0}$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. The definition of quasi-compactness applied to this affine test gives that $P_0=X_{i_0}\times_{Y_{i_0}}V_0$ is quasi-compact. Apply the same affine-atlas lemma to $P_0$ to obtain an affine scheme $U_0$ and a representable surjective etale map $U_0\to P_0$. Thus no scheme hypothesis on $X_{i_0}$ or $Y_{i_0}$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 07SL (lemma-descend-etale), proof, choice of the two affine charts; Tag 073B (lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence), part (1), and Tag 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover).

proof.text: The composite $a_0:U_0\to P_0\to X_{i_0}$ is surjective etale: the second map is the base change of $b_0$, and etale coverings are preserved by base change and composition [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Write $h_0:U_0\to V_0$ for the resulting map. Its square with $f_{i_0}$ commutes. Since $f_{i_0}$ is locally of finite presentation, the chart criterion [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] gives that $h_0$ is locally of finite presentation. For every $i\geq i_0$, and for the limit base, base change of this diagram gives schemes $U_i,V_i$ (respectively $U,V$) and surjective etale vertical maps, again by permanence of etale coverings.

source.place: Tag 07SL (lemma-descend-etale), proof, chart square and its base changes; Tags 03FT/03FU/041F and 0410 (lemma-finite-presentation-local).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages] to the system $(B_i)$. Each $B_i\to B_{i_0}$ for $i\geq i_0$, and $B\to B_{i_0}$, is affine. Their pullbacks to the affine schemes $U_0$ and $V_0$ are affine morphisms by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality], so all $U_i,V_i,U,V$ are affine schemes. The last clause of the limit lemma gives $U=\varprojlim_{i\geq i_0}U_i$ and $V=\varprojlim_{i\geq i_0}V_i$. Its isomorphisms commute with the maps induced by $h_0$: both composites have the same projections to $U_0$, $V_0$ and each $B_i$, so the fibre-product and limit universal properties identify them. The transitions of $(V_i)$ are affine by base change of those of $(B_i)$.

source.place: Tag 07SL (lemma-descend-etale), proof, affineness and limit of the chart morphisms; Tag 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), parts (1)-(2), and Tag 03WI (lemma-base-change-affine).

proof.text: The limit chart map $h:U\to V$ is etale: it is the compatible chart of the etale map $f$, so apply [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts]. Now use the scheme result [lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale] with base system $(V_i)_{i\geq i_0}$ and initial morphism $h_0:U_0\to V_0$ over $V_0$. Its initial base, source and target are affine and hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; $h_0$ is locally of finite presentation by step 2, and the limit base is $V$ by step 3. The base change $U_0\times_{V_0}V_i$ identifies with $U_i=U_0\times_{B_{i_0}}B_i$: a pair $(u,(v,b))$ satisfying $h_0(u)=v$ is exactly a pair $(u,b)$ over $B_{i_0}$. The same formula holds over $B$. Thus the scheme lemma produces $i\geq i_0$ with $h_i:U_i\to V_i$ etale.

source.place: Tag 07SL (lemma-descend-etale), proof, reduction to Limits Tag 07RP (lemma-descend-etale), in Situation 081D; Tag 03XT (lemma-etale-local), clause (7).

proof.text: For this index $i$, the diagram $U_i\to V_i$ above $X_i\to Y_i$ has etale vertical maps and $U_i\to X_i$ is surjective by step 2. The single-compatible-chart criterion [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts] applied to the etale scheme morphism $h_i$ therefore shows that $f_i$ is etale, proving the assertion.

source.place: Tag 07SL (lemma-descend-etale), last inference, via Tag 03XT (lemma-etale-local), clause (8).

Step 2: trf chartwise-etale permanence gives a surjective representable etale a_0 and the base-changed charts; the chart test gives h_0 locally of finite presentation. Step 3: the projections and transitions of the limit lemma are affine, affine-locality makes U_i, V_i, U, V affine, and its last clause gives U = lim U_i and V = lim V_i (no qcqs needed). Step 4: lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale applies with base system V_i, source U_0 and target V_0 (all affine, hence qcqs). I checked that U_0 x_{V_0} V_i equals U_0 x_{B_{i0}} B_i.
